_note: v2 hook overrides for l'observatoire & météo (B32_ciel). Source hooks are kept wherever the painting shows them; these replace only hooks whose painted scene differs from the source text (or that name a printed sign or a brewery), so the card always describes what is in the picture.

fr_tempete_noun.hook: Like English 'tempest', said tahn-PEHT: a STORM blows so hard that somebody's PET poodle floats up over the weather station like a fluffy kite.
fr_tempete_noun.why: The painting shows the poodle floating up on its own, without its owner.

fr_brouillard_noun.hook: A shivering boy in a red scarf walks into a thick FOG: "Brrr! Oh, YAR!" ("broo-YAR").
fr_brouillard_noun.why: The source hook set the fog in a brewery yard; the painting shows a boy walking into a fog bank instead, which also keeps drinking out of the scene.

fr_tonnerre_noun.hook: THUNDER: a grey cloud drops a huge iron weight that lands with a BOOM, a TON ("to") of noise in the air ("NAIR").
fr_tonnerre_noun.why: The painting turns the 'ton of noise' into a real one-ton weight dropping from a cloud.

fr_foudre_noun_f.hook: A bolt of LIGHTNING strikes a little food ("FOODR") truck and makes it sparkle.
fr_foudre_noun_f.why: Paintings carry no text, so the truck has no sign to light up.

fr_aura_noun.hook: Like English 'aura', said oh-RAH: the little weather-vane cockerel shines with a golden AURA. "Oh, RAH!"
fr_aura_noun.why: The zoom shows the glowing cockerel on the stump, with no crowd below.

fr_prevision_noun.hook: Like English 'prevision' (seeing ahead), said pray-vee-ZYOHN: a crystal ball shows tomorrow's FORECAST: sunshine, then a cloud shaped like a sheep.
fr_prevision_noun.why: The painting shows the crystal ball by itself, to avoid a second girl next to the girl with cloud hair.

fr_espace_noun_f.hook: Like English 'space', said ehs-PAHS: a fox presses the SPACE bar of a giant typewriter floating in orbit.
fr_espace_noun_f.why: The painting gives the typewriter to a fox, so it is not confused with the astronaut of l'espace (masculine).

fr_univers_noun.hook: Like English 'universe', said ew-nee-VEHR: a yellow rubber duck floats through the UNIVERSE among the planets.
fr_univers_noun.why: The painting shows the duck alone, so there is only one astronaut in the room (l'espace).

fr_lune_noun.hook: Like English 'lunar', said LEWN: a LOON bird sings to the full MOON from the roof of a little stone tower.
fr_lune_noun.why: The painting puts the loon on a stone tower in the star garden, not on the observatory.

fr_star_noun.hook: Like English 'star', said STAHR: a pop STAR sings into her microphone on a little stage, under a sky full of real stars.
fr_star_noun.why: The painting shows a singer on stage, kept distinct from the red-carpet star of la vedette.

fr_deesse_noun.hook: A marble statue of an ancient GODDESS (from the old myths) stands in the garden holding up a torch whose flame curls into an S ("day-ESS").
fr_deesse_noun.why: The painting puts the statue in the star garden and draws the S as a curled flame, since the paintings carry no letters.

fr_serenite_noun.hook: Like English 'serenity', said say-ray-nee-TAY: RAY the turtle floats in the pond in total SERENITY, gazing up at the stars.
fr_serenite_noun.why: The painted turtle floats upright in the pond, not on his back.

fr_galaxie_noun.hook: Like English 'galaxy', said gah-lahk-SEE: a GALAXY swirls across the night sky like a SEA of glitter.
fr_galaxie_noun.why: The painting shows the galaxy in the open sky rather than on a planetarium dome.

fr_secheresse_noun.hook: In a DROUGHT a scarecrow in a sash dress ("saysh-REHS") stands over cracked, DRY earth beside a wilting sunflower.
fr_secheresse_noun.why: The painted scarecrow stands by the sunflower without a fan.

fr_gel_noun.hook: Like English 'gel', said ZHEHL: FROST glazes the weather hut like shiny hair GEL, its icicles slicked back into a quiff.
fr_gel_noun.why: The painting shows the frosty hut without a skating robin, so the penguin on the black ice is the only skater.

fr_ouragan_noun.hook: Like English 'ooh, rah, gone', said oo-rah-GAHN: a HURRICANE whisks the sandwiches off the picnic blanket. "OOH! It's GONE!"
fr_ouragan_noun.why: The painting shows the hurricane spiral lifting the sandwiches off an empty picnic blanket.

fr_mistral_noun.hook: Like English 'mistral', said mees-TRAHL: the MISTRAL wind streams MISS Molly's long scarf out behind her as she battles down the TRAIL.
fr_mistral_noun.why: The painting shows the scarf flying in the wind; her hat and shopping list stay put.

fr_meteorologique_adj.hook: Like English 'meteorological', said may-tay-oh-roh-loh-ZHEEK: a wise owl in spectacles checks her METEOROLOGICAL instruments, a wind vane and a rain gauge.
fr_meteorologique_adj.why: The painted instrument stand has a wind vane and a rain gauge but no thermometer.

fr_lancement_noun.hook: A toy rocket LAUNCH ("lahn-suh"): it whooshes up from a little launch pad on the hill.
fr_lancement_noun.why: The painting sets the toy launch outdoors beside the observatory.

fr_astronome_noun.hook: Like English 'astronomer', said ahs-troh-NOM: an ASTRONOMER in a woolly hat peers through a big brass telescope at a comet.
fr_astronome_noun.why: The painting has only one garden gnome (le nain), so the astronomer is drawn as a person.
